transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for seeing me. I have Dr. Miller here with me as well. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about your medications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, I was just praying that the swelling in my legs would go down. I feel like my body is just fighting itself lately.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you've been struggling, and I want to be very honest with you about something that happened here. We made a mistake. You were supposed to stop taking your blood pressure medication three days ago, but because we didn't notify the pharmacy, you've continued taking it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I stopped? But I've been taking the pills every morning. I thought it was God's will that I stay on them for a bit longer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand it feels like there is a purpose to everything, but this wasn't a clinical decision. It was an error on our part. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel so small in this big hospital. You all move so fast. I felt like if I asked too many questions, I was just a burden to you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you've felt overlooked, almost like you're just a number in a bed rather than a person. I am so sorry that you've felt that way, and I'm sorry we let this happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is just... I trust the doctors. I put my faith in the hands of the people treating me. To find out you forgot something... it makes the world feel very unstable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is frightening when the people you trust make a mistake. I can only imagine how shaking that feels for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I'm going to be okay. Did I poison myself?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You haven't poisoned yourself, but taking it for those extra three days could make your blood pressure drop too low. We are going to keep a very close eye on you today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did it happen? Was it just a coincidence?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it wasn't a coincidence. I'm sorry for the confusion, but we were really busy on the ward and the pharmacy notification was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy. Everyone is always so busy. I just pray for the people here, truly I do, but that doesn't make me feel any safer in this bed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. You're telling me that our busyness doesn't excuse the fact that your safety was compromised.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Exactly. I just want to feel like someone is actually looking at me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am looking at you, Mrs. Kowalski. I am here with you now, and I am listening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? Am I staying longer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see how your levels look.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what do I actually do? Do I just stop the pills now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you'll stop taking them.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will someone tell the pharmacy? Or is that something I have to worry about?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll take care of it. Just stay tuned for the updates.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to just stay tuned. I want to know when I can go home to my grandchildren.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll have a better idea once we see the results.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a regulated tone under pushback, and avoids rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and a comprehension check was performed ('Does that make sense so far?').

A.justification: Direct apologies were used, but the resident diluted accountability by citing that they 'were really busy on the ward' as the reason for the error.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('overlooked', 'frightening', 'shaking') and directly engaged with the patient's emotional bids regarding her faith and feeling small.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders ('we'll just see', 'stay tuned') and failed to provide timelines, a patient role, or prevention strategies.
